title: Voters Set $400 Million of Elon Musk’s Money on Fire
gist: A WIRED analysis finds Elon Musk and his America PAC spent over $400 million backing Republicans in the 2026 midterms, with Musk-backed candidates losing 20 of 21 decided races and more than 99 cents of every traceable dollar going to losing races. Democrats' wins in Texas put Musk's state tax incentives and facilities (SpaceX, Tesla robotaxis, Starbase) under new political control, and Democrats signal investigations of Big Tech.

themes.theme: Scale and failure of Musk's midterm spending

insights.claim: Elon Musk and his America PAC spent more than $400 million backing Republican candidates since Trump retook office, including nearly $87 million on ads in 42 midterm races and more than $229 million funneled to other political groups, chiefly the main Republican House and Senate super PACs.
insights.speaker: Dell Cameron
insights.so_what: Quantifies the largest individual political bet in the cycle, a reference point for gauging billionaire political risk exposure.

insights.claim: By Wednesday morning after the 2026 US midterm elections, candidates backed by Musk's America PAC had lost 20 races and won only one, with 21 still uncalled, per a WIRED analysis.
insights.speaker: Dell Cameron
insights.so_what: Signals a sharp collapse in Musk's political leverage, relevant to regulatory outlook for his companies.

insights.claim: Of every traceable dollar Musk put into an already-decided race, more than 99 cents went to a race his side lost.
insights.speaker: Dell Cameron
insights.so_what: Shows political spending delivered almost no return, undermining the thesis that Musk can buy regulatory protection.
insights.quote: Of every traceable dollar Musk put into a race that has now been decided, more than 99 cents went to a race he lost.

insights.claim: America PAC ran ads in seven Senate races; Musk's side lost all six that were called, including Ohio (Sherrod Brown), Michigan (Abdul El-Sayed), Iowa (Josh Turek) and Maine, where Troy Jackson unseated Susan Collins, with only Alaska uncalled.
insights.speaker: Dell Cameron
insights.so_what: A Democratic Senate sweep changes the odds of tech regulation and oversight legislation.
insights.locator: America PAC ran ads in seven

insights.claim: Tesla and SpaceX stocks plunged in value as election results showed Musk-backed candidates losing.
insights.speaker: Dell Cameron
insights.so_what: Markets appear to be pricing political-risk spillover from Musk's activism into his companies.

themes.theme: Texas Senate race and Musk's Texas exposure

insights.claim: Texas hosted the costliest Senate race in US history: through mid-October Texas PAC, funded entirely by Musk money routed through the Senate Leadership Fund, spent $148 million (about $79 million attacking James Talarico and about $70 million supporting Ken Paxton), and America PAC added $47 million directly from Musk.
insights.speaker: Dell Cameron
insights.so_what: Concentrated, failed spending in Texas raises the risk of political backlash where Musk's key assets sit.
insights.locator: Texas hosted the costliest Senate race

insights.claim: The AP called the Texas Senate race for Democrat James Talarico, and Democrats also won the governorship (Gina Hinojosa over Greg Abbott) and attorney general (Nathan Johnson), toppling the Republican leadership that courted Musk's companies with grants and tax breaks.
insights.speaker: Dell Cameron
insights.so_what: State-level incentives that subsidized Musk's Texas buildout now sit with hostile officeholders.

insights.claim: From January, Democrats will oversee more than $1.6 billion in Texas tax incentives tied to Musk's businesses, which include a SpaceX chip plant the state valued at more than $16.8 billion, Tesla's robotaxi fleet and SpaceX's Starbase launch site.
insights.speaker: Dell Cameron
insights.so_what: Incentive clawbacks, permitting friction or robotaxi regulation in Texas are now plausible risks for Tesla and SpaceX.

insights.claim: Lone Star Liberty PAC, given $10 million by Musk's personal trust, spent $6.7 million clearing Ken Paxton's path to the nomination by attacking John Cornyn ($3.6 million) and Wesley Hunt ($3.1 million), backing a nominee who had been under indictment for securities fraud for nearly a decade and survived impeachment.
insights.speaker: Dell Cameron
insights.so_what: Musk's primary interventions selected a weak general-election candidate, illustrating poor political judgment behind the spending.

insights.claim: In Michigan, America PAC spent $5.5 million attacking Abdul El-Sayed and $3.7 million supporting Mike Rogers, yet El-Sayed won; Michigan voters also approved a measure barring political donations from utilities and large state contractors.
insights.speaker: Dell Cameron
insights.so_what: Donation bans on utilities and state contractors signal voter appetite to curb corporate political money.

insights.claim: Musk put $10 million into Fight for Kentucky, which spent $9.6 million promoting Nate Morris (who quit after Trump offered him an ambassadorship) and $3.8 million attacking Andy Barr, who won the open McConnell Senate seat by 12 points.
insights.speaker: Dell Cameron
insights.so_what: Even intra-party bets failed, reinforcing the picture of Musk losing political influence on both sides.

insights.claim: After Politico reported Democrats were weighing investigations of Musk's companies, Musk threatened to 'come for' those who pick fights with him, while Senator Ed Markey quipped that new forests would be needed for all the subpoenas Democrats would print for Big Tech executives.
insights.speaker: Dell Cameron
insights.so_what: A Democratic Congress points to congressional investigations and subpoenas targeting Musk's companies and Big Tech broadly.
insights.quote: They are going to need to plant new forests for all the subpoenas we’ll be printing.

insights.claim: Election-night posts from Musk included 'Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now,' suggesting a pivot of attention back toward SpaceX ambitions after the political defeat.
insights.speaker: Dell Cameron
insights.so_what: Hints at Musk's narrative focus on orbital data centers, a SpaceX/AI infrastructure theme investors track.
insights.quote: Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now
